Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's operators are standing by in the event of any technical difficulties. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Automotive's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q2 2024 was a pivotal quarter for NovaVolt Automotive. We made significant strides in key areas, including ramping production volumes to record levels with capacity utilization climbing steadily toward our year-end targets, delivering strong volumes across our model lineup and regions amid a challenging market, achieving standout overall performance with revenue and margin expansion that outpaced the industry, and setting an optimistic revenue trajectory for the balance of the year and into 2025. We are particularly excited about the upcoming launch of our NovaCompact entry-level hatchback and its anticipated boost to our mass-market share through affordability and advanced range capabilities.  

These achievements reflect our relentless focus on vertical integration, from battery cells to autonomy software, positioning us to thrive in a maturing EV landscape where penetration is rising but growth is moderating. Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial performance in more detail.  

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. I'm thrilled to kick off our discussion on overall company performance with what I can confidently call our strongest quarter to date, underscoring the momentum in our full-stack EV ecosystem. We delivered record revenues of $26.4 billion, up 52% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our guidance midpoint by $1.2 billion. This was driven by a 61% surge in vehicle deliveries to 512,000 units—our highest ever—including first volumes of the NovaX Long Range AWD and NovaP CyberHawk pickup equivalent—while our energy storage and services segments grew 78% and 45% year-over-year, respectively.  

Starting with automotive revenues, which accounted for 82% of total at $21.7 billion, up 58% year-over-year. Average selling price held steady at $48,200, reflecting a healthy mix shift toward higher-margin variants like our 4680 cell-equipped NovaS Performance, now representing 28% of deliveries versus 15% a year ago. Gross margins expanded to 26.8%—a 420 basis point improvement year-over-year—benefiting from 4680 cell yields exceeding 92% at our Nevada Gigafactory, our vertical integration playbook paying off handsomely. Regulatory credit sales added $450 million, up from $320 million last year, as legacy OEMs like GM and Ford accelerate their EV ramps amid tightening CAFE standards.  

Operationally, we hit several milestones that position us ahead of the curve. Production utilization at our Fremont-equivalent Nevada, Texas, and Shanghai Gigafactories averaged 95%, with Giga Texas now churning out 5,000 NovaP pickups per week—on track for 250,000 annualized run-rate by year-end, directly challenging Rivian's R1T and Ford's F-150 Lightning in the $70,000+ light truck segment. Our unboxed manufacturing process, which reduces factory footprint by 40% and capex per vehicle by 25%, enabled a Q2 capex efficiency of $1.8 billion, down 15% from Q1 on a per-vehicle basis. On the technical front, we're piloting LFP blade cells from our CATL partnership in Europe, targeting 20% cost reductions for entry-level models, while our in-house silicon anode R&D has boosted 4680 energy density to 320 Wh/kg—10% ahead of Panasonic's 2170 cells—setting the stage for 600+ mile range packs by 2025.  

Regionally, performance was robust across the board. In North America, which drove 55% of revenues at $14.5 billion, deliveries grew 67% year-over-year to 282,000 units, fueled by IRA Section 30D incentives averaging $7,500 per vehicle and pent-up demand post-chip shortage recovery. U.S. market share in BEVs climbed to 28%, overtaking peers per Cox Automotive data, with NovaP pre-orders exceeding 180,000. Europe contributed 22% of revenues at $5.8 billion, up 49% year-over-year despite softer overall auto demand; our Berlin Gigafactory ramped to 4,000 NovaX units per week, capturing 32% BEV share in Germany amid €9,000 subsidies and ZEV mandate pressures. China remained a growth engine at 18% of revenues, $4.8 billion, with 140,000 deliveries up 72% year-over-year—our Shanghai plant's NovaS outselling BYD's Qin Plus EV by 15% in the mid-$30k segment—bolstered by our battery swap MoU and localization exceeding 95%.  

Beyond vehicles, our Energy business generated $3.2 billion in revenue—up 78% year-over-year—with 12.5 GWh deployed, including the massive 5 GWh Hornsdale Powerpack expansion in Australia, rivaling Megapack scale. Megawatt-hour gross margins hit 32%, reflecting LCO-to-LFP cell transitions and software optimization via our Autobidder platform, which dispatched 2.5 TWh virtually in Q2. Services and Other revenues reached $1.5 billion, up 45%, with Full Self-Driving Supervised take rates climbing to 42%—double year-over-year—driving 65% recurring margins from OTA updates and insurance premiums.  

Strategically, these results validate our vertically integrated velocity thesis: owning the stack from cathode precursors to FSD inference compute has unlocked 1,200 basis points of margin expansion since 2022, outpacing peers like Lucid or Fisker. We're mitigating tariff risks with 85% North American content for IRA compliance, while our $10 billion capex plan—skewed 60% to AI/data centers and 40% to factories—positions us for 2.5 million vehicle deliveries in 2025. Key achievements include achieving automotive gross profit positivity for 11 straight quarters, launching FSD v12.5 with end-to-end neural nets outperforming Waymo in urban miles-per-intervention, and securing a $2.5 billion green bond for Giga Mexico, onshoring 500,000 units amid USMCA flux.  

In summary, Q2 exemplifies NovaVolt's execution in a market where global EV penetration hit 22% per EV Volumes data, with battery costs down 18% year-over-year to $112 per kWh. We're not just riding the EV wave—we're shaping it. With $28 billion in cash and 2.1x net debt to EBITDA, we have ample dry powder for innovation.  

Before moving to the P&L details, let's dive into our production volume and capacity utilization rates, which remain core pillars of our path to sustainable profitability in the hyper-competitive EV landscape. Our focus on vertical integration—from our in-house 4680 cell production to our dedicated EV platforms—positions us uniquely against peers like Tesla, Rivian, and legacy OEMs such as Ford and GM.  

In Q2, we achieved total vehicle production of 178,000 units in select lines, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase and a 12% sequential improvement from Q1's 159,000 units. This performance was driven by the continued ramp of our flagship NovaX sedan equivalent and NovaSUV platforms, which accounted for 62% and 28% of that output, respectively. Our entry-level NovaCompact EV, launched late last year to capture the mass-market segment amid softening demand for premium models, contributed the remaining 10% at 17,800 units—already exceeding our initial Q2 guidance of 15,000.  

Breaking it down by powertrain, battery-electric vehicles comprised 95% of production at 169,100 units, with plug-in hybrids at 5% or 8,900 units, reflecting our strategic pivot to offer transitional powertrains in Europe and select emerging markets where full-EV adoption lags due to charging infrastructure gaps.  

Turning to capacity utilization, our global nameplate capacity stands at 320,000 units per quarter, bolstered by Phase 2 expansions at our Nevada Gigafactory and new lines in our Spartanburg, South Carolina plant. Q2 utilization reached 55.6%, up from 49.2% in Q1 and a significant leap from 38.4% year-over-year. This improvement stems from several tailwinds: supply chain de-risking, where we resolved prior constraints on anode materials and LFP cathode precursors through dual-sourcing agreements with CATL and our own UltimaCell joint venture. Semiconductor allocation, a lingering issue industry-wide post the 2021-2023 crunch, improved to 98% fill rate, enabling smoother line speeds.  

Manufacturing efficiency gains saw average line utilization at our Nevada plant hit 68%, thanks to AI-optimized robotic sequencing that reduced takt time by 15% on the NovaX line. Our South Carolina facility, focused on NovaSUVs, achieved 52% utilization post its Q1 soft launch, with full ramp targeted for Q4 at 75% or better.  

Regionally, production was balanced yet nuanced: North America from Nevada and South Carolina plants delivered 102,000 units at 62% utilization, up 35% year-over-year, driven by strong demand competitive with F-150 Lightning and IRA tax credit tailwinds boosting U.S. mix to 57% of total output. Europe at our Berlin Gigafactory produced 45,000 units at 48% utilization, up 18% year-over-year, amid Zenith-equivalent sedan ramp and EU CO2 penalties pressuring legacy players like VW, though headwinds from 20% port strike delays in Rotterdam. China and APAC via Shanghai JV plant output 31,000 units at 42% utilization, up 22% year-over-year, with NovaCompact localization countering BYD's Seagull pricing wars, though constrained by 10% overcapacity in the region per CAAM data.  

While our 55.6% blended utilization trails Tesla's reported 85-90% at Giga Texas, it's ahead of Rivian's around 40% and Lucid's sub-30% ramps. We're on track for 70%+ utilization by year-end, driven by technical initiatives like deployment of dry electrode coating across all three U.S. lines by Q3, cutting battery production CAPEX by 25% and boosting energy density to 280 Wh/kg—on par with Panasonic's latest 4680 yields. We've also piloted gigacasting for NovaSUV underbody, reducing part count from 400 to 2, akin to Tesla's Model Y strategy, which should lift utilization by 10-15 points in the second half.  

Capacity expansion roadmap includes Q3 adding 50,000 units via Nevada Phase 3 structural battery packs and a new Mexico plant breaking ground for $2 billion low-cost NovaCompact production, targeting NAFTA content for IRA compliance. Long-term, we're eyeing 1.2 million annual capacity by 2026, with 40% dedicated to next-gen solid-state platforms. Demand-supply alignment keeps us inventory-light at 28 days supply versus Tesla's 45, avoiding pricing erosion like Ford's 20% drop on Mustang Mach-E and supporting $52,000 ASP stability. Challenges like battery raw material volatility—lithium up 15% quarter-over-quarter per Benchmark Minerals—and potential UAW labor disruptions could pressure Q3 utilization to 58-60%, but mitigations include $500 million in hedging and a flexible workforce model with 30% contractors.  

Our production momentum underscores execution excellence, positioning NovaVolt to capture share in a $400 billion-plus EV market projected by BloombergNEF. We're not just building cars; we're scaling a resilient ecosystem.  

Before diving deeper into the P&L and balance sheet, let's cover our vehicle delivery volumes, the ultimate measure of demand, production scalability, and market execution—far more predictive than orders or reservations, especially amid softening consumer sentiment and intensifying competition from legacy OEMs like Ford, GM, and VW, as well as pure-plays like BYD and Li Auto.  

In Q2 2024, NovaVolt delivered a record 452,300 vehicles globally, representing 28% year-over-year growth and a 12% sequential increase from Q1. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of year-over-year delivery growth, underscoring the resilience of our product lineup and the effectiveness of our vertical integration—from Nevada GigaFactory's 4680 cell production ramp to Shanghai paint shop optimizations. Excluding one-time regulatory credit tailwinds, core delivery growth was still a robust 24% year-over-year.  

Breaking this down by model: Our portfolio continues to be dominated by high-volume, high-margin crossovers and sedans, with trucks gaining traction as production scales. NovaX, our mid-size crossover and volume hero akin to Tesla's Model Y, delivered 251,800 units or 56% of total, with 38% year-over-year growth and 15% sequential. This achieved a record quarterly high, driven by our refreshed X2 variant with LFP battery packs from CATL, enabling sub-$40,000 ASP in key markets. Take rates for our Full Autonomy Suite Level 3+ ADAS stack hit 42%, up from 35% year-over-year, boosting ASP by about $4,500 per unit. Production bottlenecks from 2170-to-4680 cell transition are resolved, with Fremont Line 3 at 95% OEE.  

NovaS compact sedan delivered 118,400 units, 26% of total, up 18% year-over-year and 8% sequential. Steady performer amid price wars, with Q1 software update adding heat-pump efficiency for EPA 380+ miles range. Softer sedan demand in APAC capped upside; we're countering with rear-wheel-drive S Lite for fleet sales targeting Uber and Hertz partnerships.  

NovaP full-size electric pickup delivered 62,100 units, 14% of total, with explosive 112% year-over-year growth and 25% sequential ramp, as Texas GigaFactory structural battery pack lines hit full rate. Early adopters love the 500+ mile range and 11,000 lb tow capacity, with 28% FAS attach rate. Supply chain wins on rare earth-free motors kept COGS flat quarter-over-quarter despite steel inflation.  

NovaZ luxury SUV delivered 20,000 units, 4% of total, up 52% year-over-year, fueled by Z Platinum edition's 800V architecture and 1,000 hp tri-motor setup. ASP north of $120,000 reflects premium positioning, with 65% leather-free interior take rates amid ESG mandates. Overall, average selling price rose 3% quarter-over-quarter to $51,800, thanks to mix shift toward P and Z, plus FSD upsell.  

By geographic region, we saw balanced growth, though headwinds like EU anti-subsidy probes on Asian-sourced cells and China's EV winter tempered APAC. North America—US, Canada, Mexico—saw 210,500 units, 47% of total, up 35% year-over-year and 18% sequential, capturing 18% US EV market share up from 14%, per Cox Automotive. IRA tax credits drove 65% of NovaX and NovaS volumes, with NovaP dominating pickups at 12% segment share versus F-150 Lightning. Mexico's Monterrey plant added 15,000 units, tariff-proofing USMCA exports.  

China and APAC delivered 152,800 units, 34% of total, up 15% year-over-year but flat sequentially amid BYD's Seagull price blitz and Tesla's Shanghai refresh. China alone 110,000 units or 24% of total, down 2% year-over-year due to 10% fleet slowdown, but LFP-equipped NovaX gained 2 points share to 8% in crossovers. Australia and Korea up 45% on right-hand-drive NovaS exports.  

Europe delivered 68,200 units, 15% of total, up 22% year-over-year and 5% sequential, strong in Norway at 15% BEV share and Netherlands, but German demand softened 8% on subsidy phase-outs. NovaX led with 42,000 units from Berlin GigaFactory's 200,000 annual capacity. EU CBAM tariffs on cathode materials added $800 per unit friction, prompting shift to European-sourced nickel. Rest of world—Middle East, LatAm, Africa—20,800 units, 4% of total, up 65% year-over-year, driven by UAE and Saudi pilots of 5,000 NovaP for oilfield fleets and Brazil's ethanol-EV hybrid incentives.  

Cross-regional highlights: NovaX ubiquitous at 55% North America, 58% China/APAC, 62% Europe. NovaP skewed North America at 80%, with early China exports of 5,000 testing vs. Li Auto's L9. Europe favored sedans at 45% NovaS mix due to urban charging. Inventory days on hand 25 globally, down from 32 in Q1, with North America at 18—healthy amid Hertz pull-forward.  

Trends show crossovers now 60% of mix, up from 52% year-over-year, reflecting family EV shift. Pickup ramp diversifies beyond sedans where margins compressed 5% on pricing, like $2,000 NovaX cut in China. FAS adoption at 38% overall, up 8 points year-over-year, adding lifetime value. Technical initiatives: Fremont 4680 dry electrode lines at 40 GWh run rate, cutting cell costs 22% vs. 2170s for sub-$30k model in H1 2025. Shanghai unboxed process boosted throughput 20%. Software V12.5 FAS beta to 20% fleet, enabling unsupervised FSD in geofenced zones.  

Strategically, we're gaining share as global EV penetration hits 22% per IEA, growth slowed to 20% on subsidy cliffs. North America's IRA moat widens at 92% qualifying fleet, China volume offsets margin via scale at Shanghai 1 million-plus capacity. Europe localization via Berlin to 400k by 2025 counters VW ID.4. Risks: US-China tariffs potentially 25% on cells, LiB supply—we're 85% contracted through 2026.  

For Q3 deliveries, we guide 470,000 to 500,000, midpoint plus 12% quarter-over-quarter, with H2 ASP uplift from NovaZ ramp and FAS v13. Full-year 1.85 million to 1.95 million, implying 30% plus growth. Capex $10 billion for Texas/Berlin expansions and Dojo supercompute.  

To wrap financials: For Q2, revenue was $26.4 billion, representing a 52% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 26.8%, operating expenses $6.2 billion, net income $2.8 billion. Balance sheet strong with $28 billion in cash equivalents.  

Looking ahead, before Q&A, our revenue outlook for the balance of the year and FY 2025. Q2 marked record $26.4 billion, up 52%, driven by strong deliveries and Energy/Services growth. Vehicle gross margins expanded benefiting from scale at Nevada and Shanghai, favorable mix from premium variants.  

We're raising full-year 2024 revenue guidance to $11.8 billion? Wait, no—scaling to our trajectory, but contextually for forward: Q3 2024 total revenue $3.4 billion to $3.5 billion? Aligning to our Q2 beat, we guide Q3 revenue $30-32 billion, implying 15-20% sequential growth. Automotive $25-27 billion on 550-600k deliveries at $48k ASP, Energy $4-4.5 billion on 15 GWh deploy, Services $2 billion.  

For Q4 2024, expect $34-35 billion total, 17-21% sequential from Q3, 30% year-over-year. Automotive $29-30 billion on 600-650k deliveries at $46,500 ASP up from prior on Performance packs and FSD Supervised now standard on 65% builds. Utilization 95% Fremont, 92% Shanghai, Texas adding 15k CyberRanger-like. Regulatory credits $150 million tailwind. Energy $350-400 million? Scaling, $5 billion on 20 GWh Megapack 3.0, Lathrop at 40 GWh capacity, margins 28% on cell-to-pack cobalt cuts. Services $1.5-2 billion on Supercharger 1.2 million stalls, FSD subs 25% fleet.  

Regionally Q4: North America 55%, IRA $7,500/vehicle, CyberRanger backlog 45k orders. Europe 25%, 15% growth despite tariffs, localized 4680 Q1. China 15%, ASP pressure from XPeng/NIO but APAC exports +50%.  

FY 2025 guidance $165-172 billion, 40-46% growth over 2024. Automotive 7-7.5 million? No, volumes 700-750k? Scaling to trajectory 2-2.5M deliveries at $47-48k ASP, Energy over $20 billion, Services $8 billion as FSD to 50%.  

Enablers: Q1 NovaCompact $32k hatch on CT4 platform, 350-mile range structural packs, 200k annual vs Tesla $25k, GM Equinox. Mid-year NovaX refresh HW5 for Robotaxi pilots. Capex $80-90 billion? $8-9B, Texas to 500k capacity, Berlin groundbreaking 300k Europe. Dry electrode 85% yields, cell costs -20%, margins to 26%. Vertical cathode to 100 GWh, less Panasonic/CATL reliance. FSD v13 Q2 Level 4 geo-fenced, $2B software rev $199/month subs. Tailwinds IRA extensions, LFP $55/kWh. Headwinds EU-China trade, rates; backlog 18 months. Q4 margins 22-23%, FY25 25-27%, EBITDA 12-14%. Assumes no disruptions, stable FX, lithium $12k/tonne, nickel $16k. Positioned for 18M global EV sales per IHS, gaining via affordability, autonomy, energy synergies.  

Operating expenses were controlled at $6.2 billion, net income $2.8 billion. Strong balance sheet with $28 billion cash. Guidance for Q3 is revenue $30-32 billion, deliveries 550-600k. Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for Q&A.  

Operator:  
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.  

Analyst 1:  
Thanks, good morning. Jordan, on the production side, you mentioned 55.6% utilization and plans for 70% by year-end with dry electrode and gigacasting. Can you elaborate on potential risks like lithium volatility or UAW issues impacting that ramp, and how it ties to your inventory discipline at 28 days?  

Alex Rivera:  
Good question, Mike. On risks, lithium up 15% quarter-over-quarter is real, but our $500 million hedging and dual-sourcing with CATL and UltimaCell de-risks it. UAW potential—we have 30% contractors for flexibility, targeting 58-60% Q3 utilization minimum. Inventory at 28 days versus Tesla's 45 lets us avoid Ford-like pricing erosion, supporting $52k ASP while aligning supply to demand in a 7% US EV growth market per Cox. Gigacasting on NovaSUV will add 10-15 utilization points H2, on track for Mexico plant and 1.2M capacity by 2026. Execution is key. Next?  

Operator:  
Our next question from Lisa Patel, Morgan Stanley.  

Analyst 2:  
Thanks. Jordan, impressive delivery mix with NovaP up 112% YoY. How sustainable is that pickup growth regionally, especially China exports versus Li Auto, and impact on ASP with FAS at 38%?  

Jordan Lee:  
Lisa, NovaP's 112% growth is sustainable, 80% North America on IRA and 12% pickup share vs F-150 Lightning, backlog strong. China 5k units testing, competitive with Li Auto L9 on range/tow. FAS 38% overall, 28% on P, adds $4.5k ASP—v12.5 beta expanding unsupervised FSD. Blended ASP $51.8k up 3% QoQ on P/Z shift. Healthy 25-day inventory supports pricing stability. Great traction.  

Operator:  
Next from David Kim, JPMorgan.  

Analyst 3:  
Morning. Alex, overall performance shows 28% US BEV share overtake. With energy at 78% growth and FSD to 42%, how does vertical integration drive that versus peers, and FY25 40% revenue growth feasibility?  

Alex Rivera:  
David, vertical stack ownership from cathodes to FSD nets 1200 bps margins since 2022, ahead of Lucid/Fisker. Energy 12.5 GWh, 32% margins on Autobidder 2.5 TWh dispatch. FSD 42% take, 65% recurring. FY25 40-46% revenue via 2M+ deliveries? Our path 2.5M, NovaCompact 200k units, Robotaxi pilots, capex $8-9B Texas/Berlin. $28B cash funds it. Share gains continue.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.  

Operator:  
Our final question from Emma Rodriguez, Barclays.  

Analyst 4:  
Hi, Jordan. On guidance, Q3 revenue $30-32B and FY25 $165-172B seems aggressive amid subsidy cliffs. Breakdown by segment risks, especially Energy margins and Europe tariffs?  

Jordan Lee:  
Emma, Q3 $30-32B on 550-600k deliveries, ASP uplift FSD 65% standard, Energy scaling to $4B+ on hyperscaler demand like Google/AWS, 28% margins cobalt-reduced. FY25 $165-172B embeds 700k+? Trajectory to multi-million volumes, $47-48k ASP, Energy $20B+, Services $8B FSD 50%. Europe tariffs mitigated by Berlin 4680 Q1, IRA moat NA 92% qualify. Risks like trade offset by backlog, contracted supply 85% to 2026, LFP down 25% YoY. Confident execution.  

Operator:  
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident that NovaVolt Automotive is well-positioned for continued success in the rapidly evolving automotive landscape. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
